scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Both user LANs lost cross-AS connectivity this morning: pc1
(195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 (200.1.1.2) and pc2 cannot reach
pc1. Each PC still reaches its own gateway fine. Our NOC checked
router1: its inter-AS interface eth0 shows UP and its config is
unchanged. The partner operator (AS 2) says router2's logs show
the eBGP session dropping. Find what broke.

injection.action: administratively down the inter-AS interface (eth0) on router2

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 eth0 (193.10.11.2/24, the inter-AS
  interface toward router1)
Mechanism: router2's eth0 is DOWN, so the physical/L2 path between
  the two ASes is broken at router2's side. router2 immediately
  loses its 193.10.11.0/24 connected route and its BGP route to
  195.11.14.0/24 (nexthop interface gone), and its side of the
  eBGP session drops. Traffic from pc1 toward 200.1.1.0/24 is
  blackholed on the inter-AS segment (nothing listens at
  193.10.11.2 any more), so pc1<->pc2 fails in both directions.
  Note: router1's eth0 still shows UP (the far side of the virtual
  link keeps carrier), and router1 may briefly keep showing the
  session as Established until its hold timer expires -- the
  definitive evidence is router2's eth0 being DOWN.
Localization: router2
Root cause: inter-AS link down at router2 (eth0 administratively
  down)
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring the inter-AS link back up: on router2 run `ip link set eth0 up`. The
eBGP session re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1
reaches pc2 normally. router1 needs no change -- it was healthy the whole time.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** router2's inter-AS interface eth0 — the physical/link layer of the eBGP peering link.

**Mechanism:** BGP requires a working TCP/179 session between peers. TCP uses the L2/L3 path through the eth0 link (193.10.11.1 ↔ 193.10.11.2). Because router2's eth0 is in **DOWN** state (no LOWER_UP flag, no carrier), neither SYN segments from router2 nor keepalives from router1 can traverse that segment. Router2's BGP daemon therefore stays in the **Active** state indefinitely — it can never complete the TCP handshake to open the BGP session. Router1 may momentarily hold a stale Established entry if the hold timer has not yet expired, but no traffic can actually cross the dead link.

**Localization:** The fault is on **router2**, interface **eth0** (the link toward router1). Router2's `ip addr show eth0` output shows `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` with `state DOWN` — no UP or LOWER_UP flags — while the same interface on router1 is fully UP/LOWER_UP. Router2's BGP table contains only its own prefix (200.1.1.0/24) and has no learned route for pc1's subnet (195.11.14.0/24), causing router2 to return ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" for all packets from pc2 toward pc1.

**Root cause:** Router2's eth0 interface is down (link-down / no carrier), severing the eBGP peering link between AS 1 and AS 2 and removing all cross-AS routes.

**Fix:** Bring router2's eth0 interface up: `ip link set eth0 up` on router2. Once the link is restored, the eBGP TCP session will establish, routes will be exchanged, and cross-AS connectivity between pc1 and pc2 will be restored.
